problem: "One fixed and one free gives a quarter-wave of length 2L" invites the reading that the quarter-wave itself is 2L long, which would make the effective length larger than 2L. The other three sentences in that paragraph give the effective length (Le), so this one breaks the pattern. The actual column of height L is a quarter of a sine wave; the equivalent half-sine spans 2L.
fix: "One fixed and one free gives a quarter of a sine wave over the actual height L; the equivalent half-sine spans 2L, so Le = 2L."

where: Section 2, first paragraph after the formula
problem: "the distance between points of zero bending moment changes" is true for pinned-pinned, fixed-fixed and fixed-pinned, but not for fixed-free: the fixed end carries the maximum bending moment, not zero. A student may look for a zero-moment point at the fixed end and get lost.
fix: Say that the effective length is set by the distance between points of contraflexure (zero curvature) in the buckled shape, extending the shape beyond the column if needed; for fixed-free the fixed end has maximum moment and the shape must be extended to 2L.

problem: The text writes M = Py and then says "the moment acts to bend the column back toward the straight line". M = Py is the applied moment, which increases the bow; only the internal elastic moment EI d²y/dx² is restoring. Students often misread which moment carries the minus sign.
fix: "The applied moment Py tends to increase the deflection. The internal bending moment of the section must balance it in the opposite sense, EI d²y/dx² = −P y, and that is where the minus sign comes from."
